text:
Oliver H: Heads up — I opened a PR to bump modules/gpufleet to v2.4.0 to add az_affinity and kms_key_alias. Plan on the canary cluster shows a bunch of replacements in us-west1. Can we sync before I merge? :eyes:

Raj P: what is actually causing replacements? changed instance_template or AZ ordering?

Maria S: quick skim of the plan shows availability_zones diffs on node_pools -> provider will recreate MIGs.

Oliver H: exact snippet from terraform plan: 
```
- node_pools[0].availability_zones = ["us-west1-a","us-west1-b"]
+ node_pools[0].availability_zones = ["us-west1-a","us-west1-c"]
```

Raj P: yeah changing the list contents/order = destroy+create. We tried this before, causes rolling replacement.

Ada L: options: 1) migration logic so Terraform sees no diff, 2) lifecycle.ignore_changes on the specific attribute temporarily, 3) state migration/adopt resource trick. Each has tradeoffs.

Oliver H: I don't love ignore_changes because it masks drift, but it might be safest short-term for a small canary. infra-bot ran the canary plan and shows ~12 instance replacements.

infra-bot: CI plan summary for refs/heads/gpufleet-v2.4.0-canary -> plan complete. Resources to be replaced: 12 (google_compute_instance_group_manager). No error.

Raj P: 12 replacements in canary is ok, but prod would be ~120. Need quota/maintenance window. Also a lot of throughput lost during recreates.

Maria S: conversion shim idea: compute desired_zones = concat(existing_state_zones, var.az_additions) so TF doesn't remove current AZs. That avoids replace. Could add a hidden var _previous_zones populated by our deploy pipeline for clusters with existing state.

Ada L: example local I sketched: 
```
locals {
  current_zones = try(var._previous_zones, [])
  desired_zones = distinct(concat(local.current_zones, var.az_additions))
}
module "gpufleet" {
  source = "git::ssh://git.redwood/.../modules/gpufleet?ref=v2.4.0"
  availability_zones = local.desired_zones
  # avoid broad ignore_changes; only set for attributes we can't migrate in-place
}
```

Raj P: that seems reasonable. But how do we populate _previous_zones? GitOps pipeline could read state via terraform state pull or use a small state-inspector job as part of the rollout.

sre-oncall: operational constraints: if we do any replacements in prod we must pre-request additional GPU quota in us-west1-c and schedule during low traffic. Replacements will transiently drop nodes and may break ongoing jobs.

Oliver H: cost check — rough calc: replacing 120 A100 GPUs (short window) -> instance spin/reimage cost + lost throughput ~ $3.6k and possible SLA incident. We should avoid full replace.

Maria S: rollout approach proposal: publish v2.4.0, but set gitops manifest to ref=v2.4.0-canary for 1 cluster -> run state-inspector -> if no replacements, promote to staging (2 clusters) -> then prod in 20% increments daily with buffer nodes pre-created. Also open quota ticket now for us-west1-c.

Raj P: agree. For the canary we can allow ignore_changes on availability_zones only for the module resource but remove it before promoting. That reduces risk vs ignoring full node_pools.

Ada L: small TF snippet for lifecycle we can use temporarily: 
```
resource "google_compute_instance_group_manager" "gpu_mig" {
  # ...
  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = ["target_size"] # keep minimal scope
  }
}
```

Oliver H: ok I'll: 1) hold the PR, 2) publish v2.4.0-canary branch, 3) wire a state-inspector job in the gitops pipeline to set var._previous_zones, 4) request quota for us-west1-c, and 5) coordinate a canary window with SRE.

sre-oncall: please ping #incidents for the maintenance window booking. Also add a rollback playbook (how to back out to v2.3.x).

infra-bot: opened ticket INF-1123 to track quota request to cloud provider.

Oliver H: thanks all — I'll post the PR link and the canary plan output once infra-bot finishes a full plan. :thumbsup:
